content.text:
Salesforce CLI is installed and ready on your Mac.

### What was done

1. **Installed Salesforce CLI v2.137.7** (Apple Silicon) to `~/.local/share/sf/sf/`
2. **Added symlinks** so `sf` and `sfdx` are available from `~/.local/bin/`
3. **Updated `~/.zshrc`** to put `~/.local/bin` on your `PATH`

### Verify

Open a **new terminal** (or run `source ~/.zshrc`), then:

```bash
sf --version
```

You should see: `@salesforce/cli/2.137.7 darwin-arm64 node-v22.22.3`

### Next steps

**Log in to a Salesforce org:**

```bash
# Production or Developer Edition
sf org login web --alias my-org

# Sandbox
sf org login web --alias my-sandbox --instance-url https://test.salesforce.com
```

**Create a new Salesforce DX project:**

```bash
sf project generate --name MyProject
cd MyProject
```

**Set a default org** (after logging in):

```bash
sf config set target-org my-org
```

If you want, I can also scaffold a Salesforce DX project in a specific folder or help you connect to your org.

content.text:
The official installer needs admin rights for `/usr/local/bin`. I'll use macOS's GUI password prompt to complete the system-wide install.

[REDACTED]

input.contents:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PKG="/tmp/sf-arm64.pkg"
PKG_URL="https://developer.salesforce.com/media/salesforce-cli/sf/channels/stable/sf-arm64.pkg"

if [[ ! -f "$PKG" ]]; then
  echo "Downloading Salesforce CLI installer..."
  curl -fsSL "$PKG_URL" -o "$PKG"
fi

echo "Installing Salesforce CLI to /usr/local/lib/sf (requires admin password)..."
osascript -e "do shell script \"installer -pkg '$PKG' -target /\" with administrator privileges"

echo ""
echo "Verifying installation..."
/usr/local/bin/sf --version

echo ""
echo "Salesforce CLI installed system-wide at:"
echo "  /usr/local/bin/sf"
echo "  /usr/local/bin/sfdx"
echo "  /usr/local/lib/sf/"

input.command: osascript -e 'do shell script "installer -pkg /tmp/sf-arm64.pkg -target /" with administrator privileges'
input.description: Run system installer with GUI admin prompt

content.text:
Salesforce CLI is now installed at the **system level** using the official macOS installer, so any IDE or terminal can use it without extra PATH setup.

### System install locations

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/usr/local/bin/sf` | CLI entry point (symlink) |
| `/usr/local/bin/sfdx` | Legacy alias (symlink) |
| `/usr/local/lib/sf/` | Full CLI installation |

### Why this works for all IDEs

`/usr/local/bin` is in macOS’s default system PATH (via `/etc/paths`), so apps like **Cursor**, **VS Code**, **IntelliJ**, and **Terminal** can all find `sf` without reading your shell config.

Verified with a clean PATH (no `~/.zshrc`):

```bash
/usr/local/bin/sf --version
# @salesforce/cli/2.137.7 darwin-arm64 node-v22.22.3
```

### Cleanup done

- Removed the earlier user-level install from `~/.local/share/sf`
- Removed user-level `sf`/`sfdx` symlinks from `~/.local/bin`
- Left `~/.local/bin` on your PATH for other tools (e.g. `af_watcher.sh`)

### For other IDEs

Restart the IDE after install so it picks up the system PATH. No per-IDE Salesforce CLI configuration should be needed.
